prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Create one ambitious polished panoramic 16:9 editorial fantasy illustration for the ARC Daily Digest, expanding image 1 into a NEW full GPU Valley episode. Keep its two nearly equal rival citadels and enormous owner-matched rabbits, but pull the camera back enough to show the whole active valley. Image 1 is the base world and exact current citadel/rabbit/spider arrangement. Image 2 is the authoritative full seven-character Team Turducken crew flying aboard their cyber turkey, with exactly two Yorkies; preserve those identities. Image 3 is a reference for the rich ensemble valley, distinct workshop camps, extravagant GPU siege machines, and established visual style; do NOT leave the turkey on the ground. Images 4 and 5 are individual Puget and Sorokin references for their ONE appearance each at NVARC3's camp; ignore their old card text, scores and team labels.
EDITOR'S THREE REQUIREMENTS: (1) the bunnies have grown enormous and their citadel is almost as large as Tufa's, (2) all competing camps are busy below on wild siege equipment, and Team Turducken SOARS overhead on its flying cyber turkey, (3) heat from all the GPUs is gradually thawing the valley: snow melts, streams flow, and things turn GREEN. These three stories must all be clearly visible.
COMPOSITION: grand mountain panorama with readable foreground characters and machines, snowy ridges and two citadels at rear left and rear right, a large cyber turkey banking diagonally through the central open air above the workshops, never covering the two giant rabbit faces. There are TEN distinct team presences: two summit citadels, seven ground workshop camps, and one airborne Turducken craft. Warm sunset through rose-gold clouds, glowing electronic lamps, intricate brass/copper engineering, physical GPU boards and fan arrays, whimsical coherent machinery. Lively respectful sporting competition: build and climb, no fighting, destruction or weapons firing.
SUMMITS: Tufa left, still barely the larger citadel, exactly FIVE friendly furry black spiders arranged as in image 1 and ONE Dries on his terrace. Chen right: nearly the same breadth, height and mass in comparable perspective, exactly TWO ENORMOUS rabbits rising above it, the grey-brown lop with BOTH ears down beside its face and the dark-and-white upright-eared rabbit with the broad irregular white facial blaze. Preserve their markings and cyber collars. Keep the forts separate.
AIRBORNE TEAM TURDUCKEN: one unmistakable glorious brass-and-GPU mechanical TURKEY with red wattle, wide fanned metal tail, articulated feather wings and blue ducted-fan lift, captured in full flight with a sweeping vapor trail. Nested chicken and small duck cockpit are parts of the vehicle, not extra crew. All SEVEN established characters visibly together and recognizable from image 2: Mark (bearded powerful cyber engineer with dense GPU headgear), Son (wide luminous visor, black GPU helmet), Keith (round yellow mascot, black cap/hoodie), DZ (blonde red-eyed chibi holding small pink plush bunny), NT (orange kitten in banana suit with comic tears), Choryu (grayscale cardiac-MRI display head), Herminator (silver/cobalt knight with bright blue plume) standing in for Ronen. Exactly TWO tiny Yorkies ride safely with them. Do not add Jack Cole. Give this craft enough image area that seven crew silhouettes and both dogs remain readable; flight path is over the valley, below the fort crowns.
SEVEN GROUND CAMPS, separated by paths/streams and each working on a DIFFERENT crazy machine: mtg on a spiral gondola/cableway elevator; the last dance on a colossal folding scissor bridge and wheeled ram; Grigoriy Zatravkin on a red-orange walking foundry with articulated legs; 復活の混テキスト on a violet multi-arm crystal-lattice lifting gantry; NVARC3 on a mysterious green-and-black GPU crawler/gyroscope with Puget and Sorokin, plus small anonymous opaque-visor GPU engineers (no headcount claim); artificialagencylab.com on an enormous blue concentric-ring mobile assembly; Majkel1337 on a golden fan-powered trebuchet crane. Each camp has engineers wrenching, welding or assembling. Only Puget and Sorokin get reference-based human likenesses on ground; other camps use anonymous helmeted crews with no inferred personal likeness. Small legible pennants may say 'mtg', 'THE LAST DANCE', 'GRIGORIY', 'MIXED TEXT', 'NVARC3', 'ARTIFICIAL AGENCY', 'MAJKEL1337' respectively. Symbols on the two citadel banners, no scoreboard.
THAW AND GREENING: render this as a SLOW LOCAL TRANSITION caused by working GPU heat, not instantaneous spring everywhere. Close to the exhaust vents, copper pipes, fan arrays and crowded workshops, snow thins into wet slush, dripping icicles and dark damp stones; little clear meltwater streams join a reflective river. Patchy fresh emerald grass, vivid moss and tiny alpine shoots spread around each warm camp, progressively greener near the busiest GPU machinery; little terraces of lush green around the two citadels too. Soft steam rises where warm air meets cold. Farther away untouched slopes, shaded areas and high peaks remain snowy. Make the patchwork of snow, flowing water and new green an obvious beautiful part of the picture, not a tiny incidental detail. No flames, catastrophe or environmental lecture; affectionate fantasy metaphor.
No scores, rank numbers, dates, news branding, watermarks, card frames or unrelated logos. Keep the clean scene usable for later code-drawn graphics: small quieter lower-left and upper-right areas, no faces hidden there. Preserve identities and distinct camps while prioritizing the huge bunnies, flying full-crew turkey and visibly greening valley.
